notes: Sourced from Blackmagic Design's official DeckLink tech-specs page (manufacturer authoritative) and cross-verified against B&H Photo's detailed spec table (https://www.bhphotovideo.com/c/product/1831934-REG/blackmagic_design_bdlkhcpro8k12gg2_decklink_8k_pro_g2.html/specs) for exact connector labeling (4x BNC 12G-SDI, 1x HDMI 2.1 in, 1x HDMI 2.1 out, 1x BNC Blackburst reference in, 1x DE-9/DB-9 RS-422). As of 2026, Blackmagic no longer sells a standalone non-G2 "DeckLink 8K Pro" — the only card currently shipping under that base name is the "DeckLink 8K Pro G2" (adds HDMI 2.1 mezzanine card and RS-422 vs. the original 8K Pro's HDMI 2.0/no RS-422); B&H also lists a $105 "G2 Upgrade" mezzanine card to retrofit older units. This is a full-height PCIe x8 Gen3 capture/playback card (installs in a desktop/workstation, not rack-mountable, so rackUnits omitted); the PCIe edge connector itself is the computer interface and isn't included as a port since it has no id in the given connector taxonomy. Power connector is approximated as "dc-barrel" — see port note for the caveat that the real connector is a small internal DC power cable/connector, not a literal barrel jack.

ports.name: Ref In (Tri-Sync/Black Burst)
ports.note: Reference/genlock input, tri-level sync or black burst; not a bandwidth-graded video signal so no grade set

ports.name: RS-422 Out
ports.note: DE-9/DB-9 deck-control port; Blackmagic labels it 'RS-422 Out' though the serial protocol is inherently bidirectional

ports.name: DC Power In
ports.note: Card ships with an internal power cable from the PC's power supply to a small connector on the board (supplementing PCIe slot power, 30W total draw). Not a literal barrel jack — 'dc-barrel' is the closest available id in the enumerated connector list; the real connector is a small mini-fit-style DC power connector.
